phases.name: Refresh tsx and correct the exception record

decisions.rationale: Remedy scope (update tsx in-range + correct the GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr justification) was fixed by a human at an upstream confirmation gate, including an explicit rejection of adding a pnpm.overrides entry for esbuild. Plan matches that scope exactly; no scope expansion proposed.
decisions.signalDisposition: The concerns signal fired (7 planner concerns). All were resolvable inside the pre-authorized scope and were folded into the execution brief rather than escalated; the load-bearing one (concern 1: tsx's '~0.28.0' range admits the still-vulnerable esbuild 0.28.0) was promoted to a blocking assertion requiring the resolved esbuild to be >=0.28.1.

history.name: Refresh tsx and correct the exception record
history.retryReason: The plan's prescribed `pnpm update tsx -r --lockfile-only` was rejected by the Task 3 integrity gate (assertion D: unrelated re-resolution, including a typescript@6.0.3 admitted via transitive peers). Discarded unmodified, then re-executed with a corrected mechanism: raise the three tsx floors, then plain `pnpm install --lockfile-only`.
history.integrationNote: Spec declares every Integration Point 'None' — no entry point, registration, doc update, ADR, or knowledge-graph enrichment derived. Verified by inspection, no separate integration task.
history.reviewDisposition: Both important findings were plan-record accuracy (the plan still asserted the discarded mechanism in its blocking acceptance criteria, and still recorded a falsified 'no changeset required' assumption). Both fixed in commit c4be58756, along with suggestions S1 and S3. S2 (patch vs empty changeset for a devDependency-only change) was considered and kept as patch to match existing practice; the trade-off is recorded in the proposal and the PR body.

gates.testNote: packages/burn/tests/bin-startup.test.ts is a load-sensitive startup ratio test with a 30s timeout; it is flaky on a loaded machine independent of this change (identical post-change tree: 30007ms timeout, then 2284ms pass; base commit: 24338ms). packages/burn is built by tsup on esbuild 0.27.7, untouched here, and its binary runs under plain node, not tsx.

lockfileAssertions.overridesBlock: byte-identical to base, 23 entries, sha256 a0fdc657261e442a966b59413ecae13a70b239436d45b9458136c85d494d51c4 on both sides
lockfileAssertions.overriddenVersionsSpotCheck: undici@7.29.0, hono@4.13.1, qs@6.15.3, tmp@0.2.7, nanoid@3.3.18 all still resolve
lockfileAssertions.diffScope: confined to tsx, esbuild, 26 @esbuild/* platform packages, and tsx's own get-tsconfig/resolve-pkg-maps (dropped); tsup/vite/postcss-load-config appear as peer-tag retags only, versions unchanged
lockfileAssertions.esbuildUnderTsx: 0.28.2 (>=0.28.1 required; ~0.28.0 would also admit the still-vulnerable 0.28.0)

outcome.note: GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr remains accepted and is still reported by pnpm audit after this change. tsup 8.5.1 (latest) declares esbuild ^0.27.0, so a vulnerable 0.27.7 copy still resolves via tsup and bundle-require. This is the intended outcome; no pnpm.overrides entry for esbuild was added, per an explicit human rejection.
